name: mab-mixed
description: Classical MAB with rewards that follow no single family: 10 instances with 10 arms, each arm a random mixture of 2 or 3 components (Bernoulli, Beta, uniform, Gaussian clipped to [0, 1]), gap >= 0.05, 2 runs each. Policies built for Bernoulli (KL-UCB, Bernoulli Thompson Sampling) or Gaussian rewards (UCB1-Normal, Gaussian Thompson Sampling) against distribution-free and variance-aware ones. Theoretical defaults.

policies.label: UCBV
notes: zeta=1.2 (any zeta > 1 keeps the bound of Theorem 4)

policies.label: UCBV2
notes: rho=2.0 (the proofs of Theorems 7 and 10 of Fan et al. need rho >= 3263; Proposition 1 needs rho > 1)

notes: zeta=1.2 (any zeta > 1 keeps the bound of Theorem 4)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Some policies used the **values from their papers**: alpha=1 for UCB1, UCB1Tuned, UCB1Normal, UCBV, UCBV2, UCBMinV1 and UCBMinV2; c=3 for KLUCB. These values are safe in theory, except for UCB1Tuned: it has **no regret guarantee** (see below). In practice, they often **explore too much**. The regret can then be higher than with tuned values.
notices.todo: Search the best values with param_grid=True. Or set them yourself, e.g. UCB1(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: No regret guarantee
notices.text: UCB1Tuned has **no proven regret bound**: Auer et al. (2002) prove none. Its results can still be good, but nothing bounds its regret.
notices.default: Policies as in their papers: no projection, no buckets, no k-means (n_components=None, n_buckets=None, user_model="shared").
notices.todo: For a regret bound, pick a policy that has one (its docstring says), or turn off its heuristic option.

notices.title: Values with no theoretical choice
notices.text: Some policies kept defaults with **no value from theory**: zeta=1.2 (any zeta > 1 keeps the bound of Theorem 4) for UCBV and UCBMinV1; rho=2.0 (the proofs of Theorems 7 and 10 of Fan et al. need rho >= 3263; Proposition 1 needs rho > 1) for UCBV2 and UCBMinV2. Other values can give a lower or a higher regret.
notices.default: These values (each policy's docstring explains them).
